newsitem.title: USA: China not serious on joining WTO - USTR Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: China not serious on joining WTO - USTR Barshefsky.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Thursday that despite strong rhetoric to the contrary, China is not taking serious action on its bid to join the World Trade Organization.
"They have not shown a serious intent in getting into the WTO," Barshefsky told a Seattle business group.

She said that China's rhetoric about joining the WTO has not been matched by serious action on market reforms and other issues the United States and other trading partners view as necessary before China can be allowed into the world trading forum.
Barshefsky told the group that it is important for China, which has one of the fastest growing economies in the world, to become a member of the WTO but only on a "commercially meaningful" basis.
Chinese Trade Minister Wu Yi is in Washington, D.C., this week to attend a U.S.-China Joint Commission on Commerce and Trade meeting.

Barshefsky, who is in Seattle, Wash., to attend a quadrilateral trade ministers meeting, said she will be unable to meet with Wu. Barshefsky told reporters she and Wu tried to work out a meeting but their schedules would not allow it.
Barshefsky plans to meet Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo Sunday night in Washington, D.C. to discuss a dispute between the two countries over insurance deregulation in Japan.

Kubo wrote Barshefsky this week telling her that a plan to allow subsidiaries of Japanese insurance companies into the so-called third sector specialty insurance market will not go forward on October 1 as planned.

Barshefsky said she was pleased by the tone of the letter but had some concerns about individual points raised by Kubo. She said the Sunday evening discussion would not be a negotiating session and that she did not see a resolution of the dispute in the near term.
